newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - German unemployment reaches 3.939 mln in August.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - German unemployment reaches 3.939 mln in August.

text.p: Unemployment remained high in Germany in August as the number of jobless rose 14,000 to 3.939 million on a seasonally adjusted basis, the Federal Labour Office said.
The unemployment rate, based on unadjusted data, was unchanged at 10.2 percent. The unadjusted number of unemployed was 3.902 million, down from 3.912 million in July.
Labour Office President Bernhard Jagoda said the labour market remained weak, but should show a seasonal improvement in September.

"The decline (in unadjusted unemployment in August) was limited to east Germany, where vacations have ended. Nothing has changed in the economically subdued development and the structural burdens," Jagoda said.
"September is traditionally more favourable than August because all the summer holidays are over. I believe that the September figures will be better than August."
Jagoda was hesitant, however, to forecast when unemployment would begin to benefit from the economic upturn seen in the second quarter, when gross domestic product expanded 1.5 percent.
"Unemployment figures tend to be a late indicator, and we know it won't be just a couple of weeks (before we see and impact)."

In west Germany, seasonally adjusted unemployment rose 26,000 to 2.806 million in August, and the unemployment rate was unchanged at 9.0 percent. In east Germany the number of jobless fell 12,000 to 1.133 million. The unemployment rate was 15.0 percent, down from 15.4 percent.
